title: Release eng checklist: profile pack versioning, changelog discipline, LTS + backport policy
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Context
- runtime-1.22 introduces the Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (H100/L40S defaults; B200 gated/explicit).
- We need release-engineering rules that keep profile behavior predictable and reversible across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and that reduce config drift across branches.

Goal
Ship a concrete release engineering checklist for the profile pack, covering:
1) Versioning scheme for the pack artifact + schema
2) Changelog requirements and where they live
3) LTS branch strategy for runtime + profile packs
4) Backport policy for profile fixes (what qualifies, who approves, how to test)

Deliverables
A) Checklist (this ticket)
- A single checklist doc embedded here (and mirrored in the runtime-1.22 go/no-go email / release plan) that release managers can execute.
- Clear “stop ship” criteria when the checklist is incomplete.

B) Decisions to lock
- Profile pack versioning and compatibility semantics (including B200 hard gate behavior).
- What gets backported to LTS vs forward-only.

C) Implementation follow-ups (if gaps)
- If we lack enforcement (CI, changelog validation, golden snapshots), open follow-up ENG issues with owners.


Proposed Release Engineering Checklist (draft)

1) Versioning
1.1 Artifact names
- runtime: runtime-1.22.x (existing)
- profile pack: profiles-pack vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (stored as config artifact consumed by runtime)
- schema: schema vMAJOR.MINOR (schema changes should be rarer; patch for clarification-only changes)

1.2 Semantics
- MAJOR: breaking change in profile schema or selection semantics; requires explicit opt-in for Dedicated/Private; Hosted canary first; requires updated docs for all supported SKUs.
- MINOR: additive profile fields or new profile IDs (e.g., new attention kernel variant), or tuned defaults that may shift latency/throughput tradeoffs; requires perf-canary gating + SRE sign-off for Hosted default changes.
- PATCH: bugfixes (e.g., incorrect fallback condition, unsafe headroom threshold) that should not change expected behavior beyond fixing a defect; still must include benchmark evidence and a rollback note.

1.3 Compatibility matrix requirements
Every profile pack release must include:
- supported GPU SKU(s): H100 (SXM/PCIe where relevant), L40S, B200 (preview)
- minimum driver + CUDA baseline per SKU, and explicit “known-bad” combos
- MIG policy assumption (if relevant) and behavior when mismatch is detected

1.4 B200 gating
- B200 remains “explicit profile_version required” until Infra declares baseline driver/CUDA stable and SRE approves default enabling.
- Runtime behavior on B200 without explicit pack pin: refuse unsafe defaults and surface a clear error + action (pin version / upgrade driver).

2) Changelog discipline
2.1 Where changelog lives
- Primary: runtime release notes (runtime-1.22) include a “Profiles Pack” section.
- Secondary: profiles-pack CHANGELOG.md equivalent in the profile pack repo/module (or generated page) is the source of truth; runtime release notes should link to it.

2.2 Required changelog fields per profile pack version
- Summary (1–2 lines)
- Affected SKUs (H100/L40S/B200)
- Default changes (explicit knob deltas; batch/concurrency/KV headroom/kernel variant)
- Expected behavior changes (p95/p99 tradeoffs, throughput deltas, memory headroom adjustments)
- Risk assessment (tail latency risk, OOM risk, fallback risk)
- Rollback instructions (how to pin previous profile_version; how to disable feature flag in Hosted)
- Benchmark evidence: link to benchmark-lab run IDs and commit SHA(s)
- Observability notes: any new metrics/tags required to validate

2.3 Changelog gates
- No profile pack version may be promoted to “default in Hosted” without:
  - perf-canary comparison run against previous default
  - SRE sign-off that dashboards/alerts are in place
  - clear rollback procedure documented

3) LTS branch strategy
3.1 Branch definitions
- runtime mainline: receives new profiles pack versions + feature work
- runtime LTS branch (e.g., runtime-1.22-lts): receives only critical fixes that meet backport policy
- profile pack release lines:
  - latest: current default candidates for Hosted
  - lts-maintenance: patch-only line for customers pinned to runtime-1.22-lts (if we cannot safely consume latest due to interface/behavior differences)

3.2 Pinning rules by deployment mode
- Hosted: Redwood controls defaults; canary cohorts first; kill-switch available.
- Dedicated: opt-in to profile pack upgrades by version; allow pinning; upgrades must include customer comms (Product) if expected behavior changes.
- Private: default to “pinned to installer/runtime shipped version”; customer may override with guardrails; warn on unsupported driver/CUDA combos.

3.3 Support window
- runtime-1.22-lts supported for 6 months (proposed); profile pack patch backports allowed during that window.

4) Backport policy for profile fixes
4.1 What qualifies for backport
Backport to runtime-1.22-lts allowed if ALL are true:
- Fixes correctness/safety (OOM due to wrong headroom default, crash, severe perf regression vs documented expected behavior)
- Low-risk, well-scoped change; no new features or SKU expansions
- Benchmark-lab shows no regression outside acceptance thresholds on supported SKUs
- Includes clear validation notes and rollback plan

4.2 What does NOT qualify
- “Nice-to-have” performance improvements that move tradeoffs (e.g., higher throughput at cost of tail latency)
- New workload buckets or scheduler strategy changes without an incident/correctness driver
- Introducing new kernel variants unless required to address a correctness issue

4.3 Required approvals
- Release Eng (Connor O’Brien)
- Runtime owner depending on area:
  - kernel: Hiro Tanaka / Grace Kim
  - scheduler: Sofia Ivanova / Marcus Reed
  - KV/memory: Omar El-Sayed / Samir Qureshi
- SRE on-call readiness sign-off: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes

4.4 Required testing artifacts
- benchmark-lab run links (H100 + L40S minimum; B200 if affected)
- perf-canary delta report (when change affects defaults)
- Schema validation + golden snapshots passing

4.5 Customer comms requirements
- Dedicated: if any customer-visible SLO impact expected, Lauren Bishop must review messaging; support runbook updated.
- Private: if upgrade requires driver/CUDA bump, include explicit installer warnings and docs.

5) Go/No-Go checklist items for runtime-1.22 (profiles)
- Profile pack version selected for runtime-1.22 GA and recorded in release notes.
- Feature flag / kill-switch in Hosted verified.
- /health and debug endpoints show active profile_id + profile_version.
- Dashboards:
  - profile adoption panel
  - p95/p99 latency by profile_id
  - scheduler_queue_ms
  - kernel_choice + kernel fallback counters
  - OOM + fragmentation signals
- Runbook updated with rollback steps and escalation contacts.

Open questions / items to resolve in this ticket
- Decide whether profile pack is released independently (separate tag cadence) or only with runtime releases.
- Confirm naming: “profiles-pack” vs “runtime-profile-pack” (avoid confusion with customer-facing ‘performance profiles’ messaging).
- Confirm LTS policy duration (6 months vs 9 months) with SRE and Product.

References
- ADR: adr-041-hardware-tuning-profiles-pack (Confluence)
- Release plan draft: Google Drive ‘runtime-1-22-profile-pack-release-plan’
- Key PRs: redwood PR-24873, PR-24881, PR-24979, PR-25037, PR-25014, PR-24944
- perf-canary PR-388; benchmark-lab PR-913
